project.name: dcnet-flow
project.description: DCNET Flow is a comprehensive business management platform combining CRM, Sales, Inventory, Accounting, and specialized business modules. Built on Frappe v16 and ERPNext v16, it provides an integrated ERP system with custom applications (dcnet_apps) layered on top of the ERPNext core (dcnet_core). The platform targets two separate company deployments sharing a common codebase, backed by MariaDB and Redis.

tour.title: Project Entry Points & App Architecture
tour.description: Every Frappe app begins with hooks.py, which registers the app's doctypes, scheduled tasks, fixtures, and event handlers with the framework. The DCNET project has two apps: dcnet_core (a customized ERPNext) and dcnet_apps (custom business modules). The ERPNext __init__.py bootstraps shared utilities like get_default_company() used across all modules. Understanding hooks.py is essential because Frappe uses no traditional imports — instead, it dynamically discovers modules through these hook registrations.
tour.languageLesson: Python pattern: Frappe apps use declarative dicts in hooks.py (e.g., doc_events, scheduler_events) rather than decorators or imports. The framework reads these at runtime to wire everything together.

tour.title: DocType Anatomy — The Account Example
tour.description: A DocType is Frappe's fundamental building block — equivalent to a Django model + view + controller in one package. Each DocType lives in its own folder with a JSON schema definition, a Python controller (.py) for server-side logic, and a JavaScript file (.js) for client-side UI behavior. The Account DocType is a tree-structured document that forms the Chart of Accounts hierarchy, making it an excellent example of Frappe's tree DocType pattern with parent-child relationships.
tour.languageLesson: Python pattern: DocType controllers inherit from frappe.model.document.Document. Methods like validate(), before_save(), on_update() are lifecycle hooks called automatically by the framework — you never call them directly.

tour.title: Chart of Accounts & Vietnamese Accounting Setup
tour.description: ERPNext ships with verified Charts of Accounts for many countries. The chart_of_accounts.py module handles importing account trees from structured Python dicts or CSV files. For DCNET, Vietnamese accounting follows Circular 200/2014/TT-BTC with 254 accounts. The ChartOfAccountsImporter DocType provides a UI to upload custom COA CSVs, which is how DCNET loads its customized Vietnamese chart with accounts like 1561 (Inventory), 131 (Debtors), and 331 (Creditors).
tour.languageLesson: Python pattern: ERPNext stores chart templates as nested OrderedDicts where keys are account names and values contain account_number, account_type, and children. This recursive structure mirrors the tree DocType storage.

tour.title: GL Entry — The Heart of Double-Entry Accounting
tour.description: Every financial transaction in ERPNext ultimately creates GL (General Ledger) Entries — the atomic unit of double-entry bookkeeping. When a Sales Invoice is submitted, gl_entry.py creates debit/credit pairs (e.g., Debit 131 Receivables, Credit 5111 Revenue). The Journal Entry DocType provides manual GL posting capability. Understanding GL Entry is critical because it is the convergence point where sales, purchases, payments, and inventory all meet in the accounting ledger.
tour.languageLesson: Python pattern: GL Entry uses frappe.db.sql() for bulk inserts for performance, bypassing the ORM. The validate() method enforces accounting rules like debit == credit balancing before allowing submission.

tour.title: Purchase & Sales Invoice — Transaction Documents
tour.description: Purchase Invoice and Sales Invoice (via POS Invoice for retail) are the primary transaction documents that drive the business cycle. Purchase Invoice records vendor bills and creates GL entries for inventory (Debit 1561) and payables (Credit 331). POS Invoice handles point-of-sale retail transactions with real-time stock deduction. These DocTypes demonstrate ERPNext's 'submittable' document pattern where documents go through Draft -> Submitted -> Cancelled lifecycle states.
tour.languageLesson: Python pattern: Submittable DocTypes override on_submit() and on_cancel() to create/reverse GL entries and stock ledger entries. The is_submittable flag in the JSON schema enables the Draft/Submit/Cancel workflow.

tour.title: Payment Processing & Reconciliation
tour.description: Payment Entry handles all money movement — customer receipts, vendor payments, and internal transfers. It creates GL entries like Debit 1111 Cash / Credit 131 Receivables. Payment Reconciliation matches unlinked payments against invoices, essential for managing accounts receivable/payable. The Bank Reconciliation Tool imports bank statements and matches them to system transactions. Together, these three DocTypes form the cash management backbone of the ERP system.
tour.languageLesson: JavaScript pattern: payment_entry.js uses frappe.call() to invoke whitelisted Python methods (decorated with @frappe.whitelist()) for server-side calculations like exchange rate lookups — the standard Frappe client-server communication pattern.

tour.title: Pricing, Promotions & Loyalty Programs
tour.description: ERPNext's pricing engine uses Pricing Rules and Promotional Schemes to handle complex business pricing scenarios — wholesale vs retail rates, quantity-based discounts, and time-limited promotions. The utils.py in pricing_rule contains the core logic that evaluates which rules apply to a transaction. Loyalty Program manages customer points accumulation and redemption, critical for DCNET's retail sports equipment business where customer retention programs drive repeat purchases.
tour.languageLesson: Python pattern: utils.py files alongside DocTypes contain shared business logic callable from multiple places. This separation keeps controllers focused on document lifecycle while utils handle cross-cutting computations.

tour.title: Financial Reporting & Period Closing
tour.description: The Financial Report Engine generates balance sheets, P&L statements, and custom financial reports by querying GL entries across accounting periods. Period Closing Voucher handles year-end closing by transferring P&L balances to retained earnings. Budget DocType enables expense control by setting limits per cost center. These modules represent the 'read' side of accounting — aggregating all the GL entries created by transactions into meaningful business intelligence.
tour.languageLesson: Python pattern: Report engines use frappe.db.sql() with complex JOINs and GROUP BY for aggregation rather than ORM queries. Financial reports often return (columns, data, message, chart) tuples for the report builder UI.

tour.title: Custom DCNET Modules — E-Invoice, Reports & Fixtures
tour.description: The dcnet_apps package extends ERPNext with Vietnam-specific features. dcnet_einvoice integrates with Vietnamese e-invoice providers (Mat Bao) for tax-compliant electronic invoicing. Custom reports like Low Stock Alert and Serial No Warranty Status address specific business needs not covered by standard ERPNext. The dcnet_fixtures system generates realistic Vietnamese test data — company names, addresses, products — enabling developers to work with meaningful sample data during development.
tour.languageLesson: Python pattern: Custom Frappe apps follow the same DocType/Report folder conventions as core apps. Reports use a standardized execute() function returning (columns, data) that the framework renders automatically.

tour.title: Development Tooling & Test Data Generation
tour.description: The dcnet_fixtures module provides a CLI-driven fixture generation system with specialized generators for Vietnamese accounting data, sales cycles, procurement, and stock management. The commands.py registers bench CLI commands (e.g., bench dcnet-fixtures generate). Each generator module creates interconnected sample data — foundation.py sets up companies and warehouses, then sales_cycle.py builds on those to create realistic order flows. The .claude/skills directory contains AI-assisted development tools for code quality and learning.
tour.languageLesson: Python pattern: Frappe CLI commands are registered via commands in hooks.py pointing to Click-decorated functions. The @click.command() decorator with @click.option() creates rich CLI interfaces that integrate seamlessly with the bench command runner.
